facts.statement: Harrytoombsia was an extinct arthrodire placoderm that lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Harrytoombsia is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Harrytoombsia have been found in Kimberley, Australia.
facts.quote: Fossils are found from Kimberley, Australia.

facts.statement: Harrytoombsia was a fast-swimming predator equipped with sharp, enamel-like blades along the outer edge of its jaws to catch prey.
facts.quote: It was a fast-swimming predator, and it had sharp blades of enamel-like material around the outer edge of the jaw for catching prey.

facts.statement: Harrytoombsia belongs to the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the larger group Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Harrytoombsia is a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The genus Harrytoombsia was described by Miles and Dennis in 1979.
Harrytoombsia lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)
